nodes.text: Definitions, Lemmas, and Proofs: A Small Mathematical Study
nodes.latex: Definitions, Lemmas, and Proofs: A Small Mathematical Study

nodes.text: This paper illustrates the hierarchy of definitions, lemmas, theorems, propositions, equations, and proofs. The results concern convergence of real sequences and provide a test case for parsers that identify formal environments and preserve structural relationships.
nodes.latex:
This paper illustrates the hierarchy of definitions, lemmas, theorems,
propositions, equations, and proofs. The results concern convergence of
real sequences and provide a test case for parsers that identify formal
environments and preserve structural relationships.

nodes.text: Preliminaries
nodes.latex: \section{Preliminaries}

nodes.text: Mathematical writing uses named environments to distinguish statements from their justifications. A definition introduces terminology, a lemma establishes an auxiliary result, and a theorem presents a result of primary interest. A proof explains why a statement follows from assumptions and previously established facts.

nodes.text: Structural Dependencies
nodes.latex: \section{Structural Dependencies}

nodes.text: The proof of the sum theorem uses the definition of convergence and the triangle inequality. The proposition uses the definition again, while the boundedness lemma is an auxiliary result that is not needed for the sum theorem. A document-processing system should not assume that every earlier statement is a dependency merely because it appears earlier.
nodes.latex:
The proof of the sum theorem uses the definition of convergence and the
triangle inequality. The proposition uses the definition again, while
the boundedness lemma is an auxiliary result that is not needed for the
sum theorem. A document-processing system should not assume that every
earlier statement is a dependency merely because it appears earlier.

nodes.text: LaTeX source order also differs from semantic dependency. A command such as \ref{lem:bounded} can link a statement to another environment, while nested environments and equations create containment relationships. A robust parser should preserve environment boundaries and extract reference links separately from parent-child structure.
nodes.latex:
LaTeX source order also differs from semantic dependency. A command such
as \verb|\ref{lem:bounded}| can link a statement to another environment,
while nested environments and equations create containment relationships.
A robust parser should preserve environment boundaries and extract
reference links separately from parent-child structure.

nodes.text: Conclusion
nodes.latex: \section{Conclusion}

nodes.text: Formal mathematical documents contain useful structural boundaries. Definitions, lemmas, theorems, and proofs can be represented as nodes, but a tree alone does not capture every logical dependency. This makes mathematical text a useful test domain for structured retrieval and selective cache management.
